demos.area: A · The company at a glance
demos.title: Executive Overview
demos.question: Which area needs attention this week?
demos.decision: Which area needs attention this week.
demos.finding: Revenue is up about 18% on the same nine months last year, and everything is on target except APAC sales and receivables.

demos.title: Sales Overview
demos.question: Is sales on its growth path, and what carries it?
demos.who: The head of sales, Monday morning.
demos.decision: Is sales on its growth path, and which categories, channels, countries and products carry it.
demos.finding: Every month this year except August runs above the same month a year earlier, most of them by about a quarter; Smart Home, the newest category, has already all but caught Office Furniture for third place.

demos.title: Sales by Country
demos.question: Where should we invest next?
demos.decision: Where to invest next: which markets carry the revenue, which carry the big orders, and which grow.
demos.finding: Germany is the largest market, Canada grows fastest (about +49%), and Japan has the largest orders.

demos.title: Sales Channels
demos.question: Which channel gets the next euro of effort?
demos.who: The e-commerce and trade sales leads, deciding the next year's channel budget.
demos.decision: Which channel gets the next euro of effort: marketplace fees, the app, the web shop or the reps.
demos.finding: The mobile app has grown from about 14% to about 28% of orders since 2024 while the marketplace has shrunk from 19% to 12%. Marketplace orders come back about twice as often as web orders (10.7% against 5.6%), and Smart Home sells mostly through the app.

demos.title: Product Performance
demos.question: Which products should we push, fix or delist?
demos.decision: Which products to push, which to fix and which to delist.
demos.finding: Products rated under 3.5 stars sell about 40% fewer units per product; the AeroDesk Pro standing desk (3.2 stars) has a 17.5% return rate since April 2026.

demos.title: Seasonality & Peak Times
demos.question: When do we staff up, and when do we run campaigns?
demos.decision: When to staff up and when to run campaigns.
demos.finding: Orders peak on Monday evenings, 19:00-21:00, with Monday 20:00 the busiest hour of the week, while sales-rep orders peak on Monday at 13:00. November is about 2.3 times an average month and the Black Friday days run about 4 times an average day; the 25th to the 27th of any month bring about 25% more orders than an average day, and August runs a third below an average month.

demos.title: Sales Pipeline
demos.question: Will we make this quarter, and is next quarter safe?
demos.decision: Will we make this quarter, is next quarter safe, and which deals and sources need attention.
demos.finding: Referral deals win about twice as often as paid-search deals (51% against 25%), and next quarter's pipeline covers 2.1 times its quota.

demos.title: Targets vs Actual
demos.question: Which region is behind plan, and since when?
demos.who: The CFO and the regional directors, at month end.
demos.decision: Which region is behind plan, and since when.
demos.finding: EMEA is at 103% of target and APAC at 85%, with NA and LATAM on plan.

demos.title: Customer Base & Growth
demos.question: Which acquisition channels to fund, and do new customers come back?
demos.decision: Which acquisition channels to fund, and whether new customers come back.
demos.finding: Referral signups more than doubled after the loyalty programme of March 2025, from about 13 a month to about 29.

demos.title: Cohort Retention
demos.question: Did what we changed make customers stay longer?
demos.who: The CFO and the growth team, every quarter.
demos.decision: Did what we changed make customers stay longer.
demos.finding: Cohorts from March 2025 still have 48% of their customers ordering around month 6, about 7 points more than the cohorts before it.

demos.title: Customer 360
demos.question: What should I raise on this call?
demos.who: An account manager, before a call.
demos.decision: What to raise on the call: the money owed, the open issues, what they buy.
demos.finding: Helix Retail Group has bought 1.6M over 31 months and pays on time 136 times out of 140 - but four invoices are overdue, the oldest of them 985 days past due.

demos.title: Website Traffic & Conversion
demos.question: Is the site converting, where do visitors drop, and which sources pay back?
demos.decision: Is the site converting, where do visitors drop, and which traffic sources pay back.
demos.finding: Mobile checkout to purchase fell from about 62% to 41% in June 2026 - a checkout bug - and was back at 62% in August; email visitors convert at 6.1%, about twice paid social's 2.7%.

demos.title: Invoices & Billing
demos.question: Is this month's billing complete and collected, and what is still open?
demos.decision: Is this month's billing complete and collected, and what is still open.
demos.finding: September billing is 1,098,189.32 - 98.9% of it from trade orders and 1.1% from Care plans - against 827,603.01 collected; 12.3% of the 1,637,606.29 still open is overdue.

demos.title: Receivables Aging & Collections
demos.question: Whom do I call today, and is collection getting worse?
demos.decision: Whom to call today, and whether collection is getting worse.
demos.finding: Helix Retail Group owes 170,829.65 past 90 days - four invoices, and the whole of the 90+ bucket; DSO averages 50.3 days over 2026 against 43.4 in 2025.

demos.title: Subscriptions: MRR & Churn
demos.question: Is recurring revenue growing, and is churn under control after the price change?
demos.decision: Whether recurring revenue is growing, and whether churn is under control after the price change.
demos.finding: February 2026 was the worst month of the year for retention - every cohort kept less of itself, and price is the reason 86 subscribers gave when they left - yet MRR is at a new high of 99,781.43, with 8,102.58 of it won back by expansion over the last 12 months.

demos.title: Profit & Margin
demos.question: Is discounting worth what it costs in margin?
demos.decision: Whether discounting is worth what it costs in margin.
demos.finding: Q4 discounting costs about six points of margin every year: the discount rate runs near 6% for three quarters and 14.5% in Q4, and margin falls from 33.49% to 27.94% in 2024 and from 35.35% to 29.03% in 2025 - every category gives ground, Laptops most of all.

demos.title: Payroll Cost
demos.question: Is payroll growing because of more people or higher pay, and where does overtime cost money?
demos.who: The HR and finance controller, monthly.
demos.decision: Whether payroll is growing because of more people or higher pay, and where overtime costs money.
demos.finding: Payroll grew because Engineering hired: 20 engineers joined in 2025 against 4 who left, 40 people became 56, and of the 17,000.63 a month the department costs more than a year ago, 23,530.06 is the extra people and -6,529.43 is pay - the new engineers came in below its average. Overtime is the other pressure and it is the warehouse's: about 180 hours a month, then 539.9 in November 2025 and 531.3 in December, 2.98 times the rest of the year.

demos.title: Headcount & Attrition
demos.question: Where do people leave, and what would have to change to keep them?
demos.decision: Where people leave, and what to change to keep them.
demos.finding: Customer Support is where people leave: 17.5% a year against 9.64% for the company over the 33 months, 12 leavers from a team that averaged 25 people, and the shortest median tenure of any department at 3.1 years - 8 of its 26 people have been there under a year. Pay is the likely reason: at L1, where 10 of those 26 sit, it pays 81.7% of what everyone else at that level is paid, a median of 27,891 against 32,270; pooled over L1 to L3 it is 92.02%.

demos.title: Inventory & Stock Health
demos.question: What do we reorder today, where does it fit, and what stock should we clear?
demos.decision: What to reorder today, where it fits, and what stock to clear.
demos.finding: 14 SKUs are below their reorder level, 4 of them in Rotterdam, and Rotterdam is the warehouse with no room left: 94% of capacity against 71% in Frankfurt and 52% in Sao Paulo. 62,110.83 sits in 9 slow movers that have not sold in 90 days, none of them worth more than 6,979.31 on its own, and every one of them is in a different building - so the money to free is spread thin while the space problem is in one place.

demos.title: Fulfillment & Delivery
demos.question: Is lateness a carrier problem or a country problem, and which orders do we chase?
demos.who: The logistics manager, daily and at the carrier review.
demos.decision: Whether lateness is a carrier problem or a country problem, and which orders to chase.
demos.finding: Lateness is a carrier, not a country: SwiftPost is late 12.3% of the time against 4.28% for the other two over every delivery on the books - 12.38% against 4.25% and 3.05% in the last 90 days - and it is the worse carrier in all 18 countries where it delivers at least 60 parcels a year, from 7.56% in the Netherlands to 20% in Sweden. When it is late the parcel arrives 3.51 days late, against about a day and a half for the others, which is why its delivery-days box has the long tail.

demos.title: Support Operations
demos.question: Who works when, and which tickets do we pick up today?
demos.who: The support lead, at the daily stand-up.
demos.decision: Who works when, and which tickets get picked up today.
demos.finding: Mondays 09:00-11:00 are the peak - 1,059 tickets in those three cells against 83.33 for an average hour of the week - and urgent SLA breaches spiked in June 2026 with the checkout bug: 26.32% of that month's urgent tickets breached against 8.64% in every other month, 3.05 times the rate. The queue itself is small and slightly growing: 127 open, of which 40 are urgent or high and the oldest has been waiting 45 days, and over the 142 full weeks 13,868 tickets came in against 13,770 resolved.

demos.title: Support Quality & Agents
demos.question: Which channel should we steer customers to, and which agents need coaching?
demos.who: The head of support, at the monthly review.
demos.decision: Which channel to steer customers to, and which agents to coach.
demos.finding: Chat leaves people happiest and no faster: CSAT 4.4 on chat against 4.07 on the phone, 3.83 by email and 3.67 on the web form, while a ticket takes 60 to 63 hours to resolve whichever channel it arrives on - chat's median, 62.63 hours, is the longest of the four against the web form's 60.28. So chat buys satisfaction, not speed. Every team clears the 90% SLA target, from 90.5% in Billing to 91.5% in Technical, and the 32 agents sit between 3.86 and 4.13 CSAT, so there is no one to single out for coaching.

demos.title: Table Profile
demos.question: Can I trust this table, and which of its columns can I use?
demos.who: The analyst meeting a new table.
demos.decision: Whether the table can be trusted, and which columns can be used.
demos.finding: Pick any table and you know it in half a minute: support_tickets holds 14,000 rows over 15 columns, 476 of them opened in the last 30 days, and 4 columns have gaps - order_id is empty on 52.64% of tickets, because a ticket need not be about an order, and csat_score on 58.33%, because most people never answer the survey. Its priority column is 51.56% normal and 8.21% urgent. Point the same page at orders.total_amount and the chart turns into twenty ranges over 23,162 distinct amounts, 20,782 orders inside the first one.

demos.title: One Metric, Every Angle
demos.question: Is each of the company's five metrics where it should be, and what drives it?
demos.who: The COO, at the monthly business review, walking through the five metrics one at a time.
demos.decision: Whether each metric is where it should be, and what drives it.
demos.finding: Revenue is 17.5% up on the same span of last year and orders 27.55% up, while tickets grow 10.32% - support scales with the business rather than with the order book. Orders growing faster than revenue is the other half of that sentence: the average order is smaller than it was. November is the biggest month of the year for both, 8,273,224.34 and 3,165 orders against a May second place of 5,920,290.39, while payroll peaks in March and new customers in September. Germany leads all five metrics, revenue 3,651,821.21 of the 18,326,301.98 year to date.

demos.title: Segment vs Everyone
demos.question: Is my country different from the company as a whole, and where?
demos.who: A country manager: "is my country different?"
demos.decision: What to do differently in my market: assortment, channel, price.
demos.finding: Poland is a smaller basket and a faster market: 1,944.91 an order against 2,756.55 everywhere, returns no different at 5.93% against 5.97%, but quarterly revenue at 208.67 against the company's 139.44 since the start of 2024. It buys more Smart Home, 12.2% of its revenue against 10.58%, and a little more on the app, 21.37% of its orders against 20.55% - the assortment difference is real, the channel difference is under a point.
